title: Traffic Economics: Launch Quick-Check & Roadmap Tracker
body:
Purpose:
A compact quick-check for product ops, infra, and finance to validate the economics and user-latency posture of routes before ramping traffic. This is optimized for launches where traffic mix or model variants materially change token shape or latency (e.g., new generation models, model quantized variants, or new conversational routes).

When to use:
- Any route expecting >10k QPS-equivalent monthly traffic shift or when model variant changes tokens/request by >20%.
- During 22 week prelaunch window and first 7 days post-ramp.

High-level checklist snapshot (one-pager):
1) Set route leash: per-route daily spend cap and slow-ramp limits. Finance signs off on leash.
2) Define baseline token mix: %generation vs %embedding vs %rerank (sampled from prod logs).
3) Run quick economics sim: feed token-mix into cost estimator and get a per-1k request USD estimate and 95% CI.
4) Validate latency tail on representative prompts across regions and customer tiers.
5) Ensure rollback knob: pinned model artifact + traffic cutover script tested.

KPI tracker (compact table, copy/paste friendly):
Metric | Unit | Target | Alert | Owner | Cadence | Source
Token cost (est) | USD / 1k requests | <= $0.40 | >= $0.60 | Finance (Priya) | daily | billing + estimator
p95 inference latency | ms | <= 300 | > 380 | SRE (Diego) | 15m | traces
95th cost-per-customer | USD / customer-day | <= $12 | > $18 | Product Ops (Marta) | daily | analytics + billing
Embedding % of tokens | % tokens | <= 15% | > 30% | AppliedML (Aisha) | daily | usage logs
Cache hit ratio (prefix) | % tokens | >= 25% | < 15% | Runtime Eng (Benji) | hourly | runtime metrics
Batching efficiency | tokens/request | 1.6-3.0 | <1.2 or >4.0 | Runtime Eng (Benji) | hourly | runtime metrics
Cold-start incidence | % requests | < 4% | > 8% | Platform (Samir) | hourly | telemetry
Quality drift (launch eval set) | delta metric | no regression >0.015 | >= 0.015 | AppliedML (Aisha) | nightly prelaunch + nightly postlaunch | eval harness
Failover rate | % requests | 0% | >1% | Product Ops (Marta) | hourly | routing logs
SLO burn (24h) | % budget | < 25% | > 50% | SRE (Diego) | daily | SLO dashboard

Prelaunch 48h quick-check (operational steps):
A. Economics & capacity
- Confirm daily route leash and agreed emergency spend procedure.
- Run three short sims (low/median/high) for 1 hour each with representative prompt mix; collect cost and latency samples.
- Validate autoscaling windows and burst caps; ensure dedicated pools available if latency exceeds threshold.
- Confirm quantization/precision settings and that eval harness passes.

B. Observability & alarms
- Publish the one-pane dashboard with the KPI tracker and share with oncall.
- Configure a 15m p95 latency alert, a 1h cost spike alert, and a 4h leash breach page to finance.
- Enable sampling-level traces for first 6h of ramp and keep logs for 14 days.

C. Quality & regression
- Run the launch eval suite against candidate model + baseline; any regression > threshold requires AppliedML triage.
- Confirm structured-output or function-calling compatibility for the route.

D. Runbook & comms
- Validate rollback script and do a dry-run traffic cutover in staging.
- Owner roster for first 72h (include daytime and night deputy).
- Prewritten customer-facing note template and internal status template in Slack.

Decision gates (quick rules):
- Economics gate: projected cost at 25% ramp must be <= target band OR explicit finance waiver documented.
- Latency gate: p95 at 50% trial ramp must be < alert threshold and cold-starts not trending upward.
- Quality gate: launch eval shows no regression beyond delta; if borderline, require applied-ML mitigations.
- Observability gate: dashboard and alerts must be live and acknowledged by oncall.

Go/no-go matrix (fast):
- GO: all gates green. Ramp path: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 48h with monitoring checks between steps.
- CAUTION: one non-critical gate amber (e.g., cache slightly low). Proceed with capped ramp (max 50%) + immediate remediation plan.
- STOP: any critical gate red (cost leash breach, quality regression). Abort and rollback.

Rapid mitigations (playbook snippets):
- If cost spike detected: enable per-route rate limit, switch to lower-cost model variant, pause non-critical background jobs that trigger inference.
- If latency tail increases: move high-value customers to dedicated pool, enable prioritization policy, scale warm replicas.
- If quality regressions appear in production: pin traffic to previous model, open applied-ML investigation, and deploy hotfix canary.
- If cold-starts persist: increase warm pool, enable keep-alive pings for top prefixes.

Post-ramp 7-day activities:
- Maintain high sampling tracing for first 72h and continue daily KPI digest for 7 days.
- Fill in the Roadmap Tracker row for this route: actual cost vs forecast, latency deltas, owner notes, lessons.
- If any gate tripped, file a micro-postmortem and list remediation owners and timelines.

Notes and open items:
- Need a faster estimator for mixed embedding/generation routes that runs on daily logs and returns a 95% CI (PROJ-855).
- Explore exposing an opt-in per-route "latency SLA" in Console for premium customers (commercial interaction required).
- Determine privacy-safe way to surface per-route cost signals to customers without exposing discounts or internal pricing bands.

Owner signoffs required before ramp:
- Product Ops: Marta Liu
- Finance: Priya Srinivasan
- SRE: Diego Morales
- Runtime: Benji Carter
- Applied ML: Aisha Kapoor

Quick commands and references:
- Local sim: scripts/sim/quick_sim.sh --route payments --duration 60m --mix-file samples/mix.json
- Eval harness: tools/eval/run --suite launch-2024-q4 --model candidate --baseline pinned
- Dashboards: /console/dashboards/traffic-economics-quickcheck

Version notes:
- v0.1 (2024-10-12) initial quick-check draft
- v0.2 (2024-12-01) added leash concept and per-customer 95th cost metric

If you are the launch owner: paste this into the launch binder, run the 48h quick-check, and collect the KPI snapshot before the first traffic ramp.
